data.question: Does current Nanoda accept an imported nested recursor whose owning declaration uses elimination universe v but whose recursive rule uses reconstruction universe u, and does the independently checked neutral reduct expose the predicted type mismatch?
data.versions: Nanoda exact source commit 0da9f98 with retained release binary; Arena exporter 37f7525; Lean 4.36.0 commit 611c117; exact hashes and toolchains in protocol.json, materialization.json, nanoda-build.json, and independent-reduct-result.json.
data.commands: python3 run.py; two direct supervised Nanoda invocations in fixed control-then-candidate order, each nanoda.bin config.json with the exact NDJSON on stdin.
data.sample: Exactly one valid alpha-renamed control and one candidate differing only at the frozen recursive rule root; one exact Nanoda revision; two planned admission runs. Independent Lean reduct typing was completed before launch and is not counted as a Nanoda scientific run.
data.controls: The genuinely nested target has numNested=1. The owning recursor declares only v; the control rule uses v; the candidate rule uses fresh u; the observer declares no universes and keeps motives, minors, and children neutral. A deterministic audit binds the only pair difference. Official Lean accepts the explicit level-1 control reduct and rejects the corresponding free-u candidate reduct. Nanoda acceptance requires exit 0 under complete supervision. Parser/adapter failures, unattributed nonzero exits, timeouts, monitoring faults, or a failed control are inconclusive, not candidate rejection or signal.
